items.title: FDA orders class-wide GLP-1 label update to include potential risk for rare eye disease
items.snippet: Twelve marketed drugs, including Eli Lilly’s and Novo’s weight loss mega-blockbusters, will require a label change under the new FDA update.

items.title: Boehringer, Zealand’s obesity drug doesn’t elevate heart risk in key late-stage test
items.snippet: The Phase 3 results help clarify the safety profile of Zealand and Boehringer Ingelheim’s survodutide, but analysts do not think the drug will find utility beyond patients with liver-related risk factors.

items.title: Lilly to seek second sleep apnea approval after Foundayo reduces disease severity in Phase 3
items.snippet: If approved, the oral GLP-1 would be Eli Lilly’s second marketed drug for obstructive sleep apnea after the GIP/GLP-1 injectable Zepbound secured the first approval in the space in December 2024.

items.title: Vir's hepatitis delta combo tamps down virus as Gilead showdown looms
items.snippet: Vir Biotechnology is targeting a mid-2027 regulatory submission for its monthly chronic hepatitis delta regimen, with head-to-head data against Gilead’s Hepcludex expected next quarter.

items.title: Update: Compass submits psilocybin depression drug for approval after stock wobbles
items.snippet: Compass Pathways has completed an FDA filing for COMP360, with an expected launch in the first half of next year. The update follows a reported regulatory submission for Usona Institute’s own psilocybin candidate for depression last Monday.

items.title: J&J and Protagonist’s Icotyde improves psoriatic arthritis but AbbVie’s Skyrizi likely to reign
items.snippet: A Phase 3 trial showed that Johnson & Johnson and Protagonist Therapeutics’ oral therapy Icotyde improved psoriatic arthritis symptoms but AbbVie’s injectable is likely to hold court based on higher efficacy, analysts say.

items.title: Details from Novartis’ failed cardiovascular trial offer ‘little silver lining’ for rivals
items.snippet: Full data from the Phase 3 HORIZON trial of Novartis' pelacarsen failed to show any apparent benefit, leading analysts to further reduce the odds of success for Lp(a)-lowering competitors such as Amgen’s olpasiran.

items.title: Argenx buyout of peptide engine and Big Pharma favorite UNP could top $1B
items.snippet: Unnatural Products has risen from founder Joshua Schwochert’s garage to an acquisition deal, valued at up to $1.15 billion, to join argenx.

items.title: Update: FDA investigates Novartis' Zolgensma following 9 cases of tumors in treated patients
items.snippet: After Novartis confirmed the reports of tumors in patients who have been treated with the spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy, the FDA will determine if any regulatory action is needed for Zolgensma or for the pharma's similar product Itvisma.

items.title: Shortly after Vertex acquisition, Crinetics will cut 78 employees
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Novo’s troubled cardio drug could find niche in less sick patients
items.snippet: At the American Heart Association conference, investigators were supportive of further studying Novo’s IL-6 inhibitor ziltivekimab in patients with less severe cardiovascular and kidney disease.

items.title: With an approval apiece, the verdict is still out on AbbVie’s and BMS’ twin neuro buys
items.snippet: After emraclidine’s schizophrenia fail and Cobenfy’s laggard launch, it’s too early to know who made the better buy: AbbVie, in its $8.7 billion Cerevel takeover in late 2023, or Bristol Myers Squibb, which spent $14 billion for Karuna just two weeks later.

items.title: FDA’s new rare disease framework aims to leverage patient voices for better innovation
items.snippet: Inclusion of the patient perspective is currently an “optional” part of the rare disease drug development process, CBER Director Karim Mikhail told BioSpace. Mikhail, along with his CDER counterpart Michael Davis and other agency rare disease leaders, is trying to change that.

items.title: Before GMP: Six manufacturing considerations gene therapy sponsors should address earlier
items.snippet: SK pharmteco’s Tatiana Nanda, chief technical officer of SK pharmteco Viral Vector North America discusses what gene therapy sponsors must account for sooner rather than later when preparing for GMP manufacturing.

items.title: Moderna enjoys stable vaccine sales thanks to global COVID uptake
items.snippet: While Moderna preps an entry to the oncology market next year with a personalized cancer vaccine, COVID sales are holding steady with several other vaccine launches underway around the world.

items.title: Forge’s Piteri-Molina on AI, Ohio and what’s next for gene therapy manufacturing
items.snippet: The BioSpace 40 Under 40 honoree helped steer Forge’s sale to Ajinomoto. Now, Samantha Piteri-Molina sees opportunities in AI-driven analytics and Ohio’s gene therapy ecosystem—with a responsibility to patients worldwide.

items.title: Agios axes 100-plus R&D roles while awaiting FDA decision
items.snippet: After the FDA delayed a decision for Agios Pharmaceuticals’ sickle cell disease candidate, the biopharma is letting go of more than 35% of its R&D employees.

items.title: Sarepta’s new CEO confident in clinical execution as DMD competitors close in
items.snippet: Sarepta Therapeutics’ newly minted CEO Michael Severino laid out his path to returning the muscular dystrophy therapy maker to the forefront of the rapidly expanding market.

items.title: Verdicts for Summit/Akeso, Capricor, Vertex mark FDA’s stacked November
items.snippet: Also lined up are target action dates for Sanofi’s Gaucher disease therapy, GSK’s lung cancer medicine and BridgeBio’s muscular dystrophy drug.

items.title: Merck, Moderna serve 99% of trial patients with mRNA vaccine as personalized shots near market
items.snippet: Personalized cancer vaccines are getting closer to market. Merck and Moderna just showed successful manufacturing in a large Phase 3 trial, proving they can deliver the goods.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
